# The time field's picker throws on every pick and keeps the old time

## Context

On `dev` (`81fa6e82db`), open `examples/component/clock`, open the time field's picker and click any time. The field keeps its old value, and the page logs this once per pick:

```
TypeError: this.store.getCanonicalKey is not a function
```

Measured 2026-11-18: three errors for one click; the field stayed `10:20`. Typing a time and pressing Enter throws the same error. Found while capturing the example's cover for #21120.

## The Problem

`Neo.list.Base#getItemRecordId` (`src/list/Base.mjs:817`) calls `this.store.getCanonicalKey(itemId)` whenever `useInternalId` is false. `getCanonicalKey()` exists only on `Neo.data.Store` (`src/data/Store.mjs:1608`). The time field gives its picker list a plain `Neo.collection.Base` with `useInternalId: false` (`src/form/field/Time.mjs:118-124`), so every pick throws before the field takes the value.

It is a regression of #17717 (2026-08-24), which replaced three hand-rolled conversions with the new primitive. The replaced lines read `this.store.getKeyType?.()`, which a collection answers as well, so collection-backed lists kept working. The primitive was added to `Store` only, and the call sites lost the guard. `Neo.component.Helix` (`:830`), `Neo.component.Gallery` (`:581`) and `Neo.list.Buffered` (`:536`) carry the same unguarded call, but their usual stores are Stores.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.list.Base` supports both store kinds by design: `getKeyProperty()` reads "Support collections & stores" (`src/list/Base.mjs:822`).
- `Neo.collection.Base#getKeyType()` (`src/collection/Base.mjs:1217`) infers the key type from the first item, which is what the pre-#17717 conversion used: an integer-keyed collection parsed the DOM fragment, any other passed it through.
- `Neo.data.Store` extends `Neo.collection.Base`, so a base method is the one its existing override narrows.

## The Fix

Add `getCanonicalKey(value)` to `Neo.collection.Base`: an absent value resolves to `undefined`; in an integer-keyed collection (per `getKeyType()`) a numeric value or string parses to a number, and one that does not parse resolves to `undefined`; otherwise the value stands as its own key. `Neo.data.Store` keeps its model-aware override. No call site changes.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.collection.Base#getCanonicalKey(value)` (new) | `Neo.list.Base#getKeyProperty()`: "Support collections & stores"; the key type `getKeyType()` infers | An absent value resolves to `undefined`; an integer-keyed collection resolves a numeric value or string to a number and refuses anything else with `undefined`; any other collection keeps the value | `Neo.data.Store#getCanonicalKey()` keeps its model-aware override, unchanged | The method's JSDoc | AC-2 |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Clicking a time in `examples/component/clock`'s picker sets the field and the clock, with no page error. Checked in the browser before and after.
- [ ] AC-2: A unit spec proves `Neo.collection.Base#getCanonicalKey()` for a string-keyed collection, an integer-keyed collection (including a refused non-numeric fragment) and an absent value; and that `Neo.list.Base#getItemRecordId()` resolves an item of a collection-backed list. Both fail on `dev` without the fix.
- [ ] AC-3: The unit suites of `collection`, `data`, `list` and `form` pass.

## Out of Scope

- `Neo.data.Store#getCanonicalKey()`'s domain rules (#17716, #20928).
- Typing a time that matches no picker entry.
